clue.text: She's a grown-up and excellent learner

parts.note: someone grown-up is big
AI, read as A1, means first-rate or excellent
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Someone is described as a mature adult who learns brilliantly.
explanation.walkthrough: AI stands in for A1, first-class; 'She' is defined by a name, since an abigail was once a lady's maid and is a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Abigail is a female forename, so it can stand for a woman referred to as 'she'.

clue.text: A boundary put up for deer

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the word is reversed, reading upwards

parts.note: in cricket a six is a boundary hit over the rope

explanation.surface: A fence is erected to keep deer in.
explanation.walkthrough: A six in cricket is a boundary hit clearing the rope; reversed it gives XIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The axis, or chital, is a spotted Asian deer.

clue.text: Is follower of me associated with an Iranian city?

parts.note: in sol-fa, doh ray me is followed by fah

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a fan of theirs is connected with a city in Iran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follower of me' looks like a fan; it is the note fah that follows me in the tonic sol-fa scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Isfahan is a historic city in central Iran, once the Persian capital.

clue.text: Behave badly in a court, appearing for trial

parts.note: someone up before the magistrates is appearing for trial

explanation.surface: A defendant misbehaves in a courtroom at their trial.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to misbehave or play up.

clue.text: A period of adjustment

parts.note: a year with an extra day added to bring the calendar back into line with the sun

explanation.surface: A settling-in time after a change.
explanation.definitionFit: Every fourth year gains 29 February to correct calendar drift, a twelve-month span of correction.

clue.text: King in game of cards, say

indicators.note: say tells us to go by how the card game's name is spoken

parts.note: faro is an old gambling card game

explanation.surface: A king turns up in the middle of a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: Faro, a gambling card game, is pronounced like the title of the Egyptian ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: The rulers of ancient Egypt bore this title, so it names a monarch.

clue.text: Create reductions, i.e. switch in prices

indicators.note: the letters i and e are swapped within the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Bring about price cuts by changing the price list.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the I and E in PRICES gives the answer; 'reductions' looks like price cuts but means summaries.
explanation.definitionFit: To precis is to summarise, making shortened versions of a text.

clue.text: Runs into some anger in such profitable dealing

indicators.note: into means the runs letter goes inside the phrase for some

parts.note: a bit means some
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
rage is anger

explanation.surface: Someone runs into a little anger over a lucrative deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Arbitrage is profiting by buying and selling the same asset in different markets at once.

clue.text: Bird cooked and consumed in time to digest

indicators.note: consumed in means the scrambled letters are swallowed by the time word

parts.note: an age is a period of time

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are tampered with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird is cooked and eaten over a long time to aid digestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' signals the anagram and 'consumed in' the container; 'digest' is a verb meaning summarise, not eat, and 'time' is an age.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it, as a digest condenses material.

clue.text: Type of rock that contains lead, say

definitions.meaning: a loud, guitar-heavy genre of rock music
lead is an example of a dense metallic element

explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' suggests geology but is music; 'say' marks lead as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy metal names both a hard-rock genre and dense metals such as mercury or lead.

clue.text: To inspire with passion, Auntie broadcast about rich

indicators.note: about tells us the scrambled letters go around the other piece
broadcast suggests the letters are scattered widely, so they are reshuffled

parts.note: rich food is fat, as in the fat of the land

explanation.surface: Auntie, the BBC's nickname, broadcasts something about wealth in order to stir passions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' signals the anagram and 'about' the container. Auntie is a nickname for the BBC, which suits the broadcasting surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To infatuate someone is to fill them with a foolish passion.

clue.text: Drill modern army, initially, in the old country

parts.note: a bur is a small dentist's drill

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A modern army is drilled in an old-fashioned land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drill' looks like an army exercise but is the dentist's bur.
explanation.definitionFit: Burma is the former name of Myanmar, so it is a country under its old name.

clue.text: New Age greeting?

parts.note: not mystical New Age talk: a greeting for someone who has just reached a new age, a year older

explanation.surface: A salutation from the world of crystals and mysticism.
explanation.definitionFit: The words wished on someone's birthday greet them on reaching a fresh number of years.

clue.text: Scientific approach applicable to light reading

definitions.text: Scientific approach applicable to light reading

parts.words: Scientific approach applicable to light reading
parts.note: not reading a book lightly: the science of taking readings of light intensity

explanation.surface: A scholarly method for easy holiday books.
explanation.definitionFit: Photometry is the measurement of luminous intensity, done with a meter giving readings.

clue.text: Applause as drink's provided on taps?

definitions.text: Applause as drink's provided on taps?

parts.words: Applause as drink's provided on taps?
parts.note: beer comes on tap, so a round of claps for drink is read as hands striking together

explanation.surface: Customers cheer when beer starts flowing from the pumps.
explanation.walkthrough: Taps are both beer taps and light blows: a clap given by the hands is applause.
explanation.definitionFit: A single strike of palms together is a basic unit of applause.

clue.text: Violent upheaval' in which many stay calm, remarkably

indicators.note: in which tells us the many letter sits inside the rearranged phrase
remarkably suggests the phrase is altered strikingly, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

explanation.surface: A great disaster in which crowds keep their cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkably' makes CATALYSM from STAY CALM, and 'in which' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataclysm is a sudden catastrophic event or upheaval, such as a flood or war.

clue.text: Please change this tree

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the letters of the word before it

explanation.surface: A polite request to alter a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapele is a West African hardwood tree related to mahogany.

clue.text: Growth of profit

parts.note: not an increase in earnings: something grown in the fields to be sold for money

explanation.surface: Rising earnings.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash crop is farm produce grown for sale rather than for the farmer's own use.

clue.text: Eager to get son released, having made a couple of points in court

definitions.text: having made a couple of points in court

indicators.note: released means the son is let go, dropped from the word

parts.note: thirsty for something means eager for it

explanation.surface: A keen player gets a boy freed after scoring in a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests law but is the tennis court: after two points won in a game a player's score is called thirty.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis scoring, love, fifteen, thirty and forty follow points won, so two points take a player to thirty.

clue.text: The sort of dealing that could get one imprisoned? Right

parts.note: someone in prison is said to be inside

explanation.surface: A kind of trading that could land someone in jail, rightly.
explanation.walkthrough: Insider dealing, trading on confidential information, is a crime that can get one jailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Insider dealing is trading using privileged company information, so the word names that kind of dealing.

clue.text: European port so long associated with North American agents

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell, so long
the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

explanation.surface: A goodbye from a port linked with spies from across the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Valencia is a Mediterranean port city in eastern Spain.

clue.text: Ice cream was examined in European house

indicators.note: in tells us one piece goes inside the house word

parts.note: casa is house in Spanish and Italian
someone who sat an exam was examined

explanation.surface: An ice cream was inspected at a home on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European house' wants a foreign word: casa in Italian or Spanish.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassata is an Italian ice cream containing candied fruit and nuts.

clue.text: Captain Hemingway associated with the sea

definitions.meaning: slang for the skipper of a ship, the boss
Santiago, Hemingway's aged fisherman in his novella paired with the sea

explanation.walkthrough: Hemingway's novella is The Old Man and the Sea; a ship's captain is informally called the old man.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors call their commander by this informal title, and it is Hemingway's elderly fisherman.

clue.text: Stop playing in this game, and one stands to lose

definitions.text: Stop playing in this game, and one stands to lose

parts.words: Stop playing in this game, and one stands to lose
parts.note: in the party game, when the music stops, the player left standing without a seat is out

explanation.surface: A game where quitting means a likely loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop playing' is the music stopping, and 'stands' is literal: whoever is left on their feet loses.
explanation.definitionFit: This children's party game removes one seat each round, eliminating whoever cannot sit when the music halts.

clue.text: I score only one half-century for this country

indicators.note: only one means of the two fifties in the score word just one survives, so one is dropped

parts.note: a tally is a score or count
a half-century is fifty, and L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A cricketer laments making just one fifty for their national side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-century' is cricket for fifty runs, here L, the Roman fifty; 'only one' keeps a single L of the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Italy is a country in southern Europe.

clue.text: Bill's master

definitions.meaning: British school slang for a schoolmaster, also a magistrate

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a beak is a schoolmaster or magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's bill is its beak, and the same word is old slang for a teacher.

clue.text: Party held back by river, for the present

indicators.note: held tells us the river encloses the other piece

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river

indicators.note: back means the party word is read in reverse

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A party is delayed by a river, for now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' signals the reversal and 'held' the container; the Tay is the longest river in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: This day, as opposed to the past or future, is the present time.

clue.text: Preserve me with weapon a boy concealed

indicators.note: concealed means the first word holds the other pieces hidden within it

parts.note: an arm is a weapon
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone is told to protect themselves while a boy hides a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserve' looks like a verb but is the noun: a jam.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a citrus jam, a kind of fruit preserve.

clue.text: One who works with wood and copper?

definitions.meaning: a worker in a timber yard
a policeman from Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters

explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the London Metropolitan Police headquarters, hence the question mark for a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Yardman covers both a labourer in a lumber yard and, jokingly, a detective of the Yard.

clue.text: In return, put tar on the stern

parts.note: to pay a ship's seam is to coat it with tar or pitch
the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A sailor tars the rear of a ship in exchange for something.
explanation.walkthrough: The nautical verb pay means to cover with tar; the stern is the back end of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Payback is a return on an outlay, or retribution given in exchange.
